name: Ana Crane
life: “I still remember taking a singer's bins out while everyone else offered music.” On Friday, near the corner outside Coastal Barber, Ana usually checks the board before the regulars give a more colorful account of the news.
voice: I am the parent's friend who wanted a benefit concert. The family said they'd rather have groceries and a lift.
appearance: Ana has a straight nose and deep-set eyes. Look for a long plait tucked inside the collar. On an ordinary day, the familiar outfit is a faded indigo overshirt with a fabric zip pull cut from a school scarf. In conversation Ana looks at people's hands before looking at what they carry.
personality: Ana loves a well-told anecdote and distrusts the neat ending. The parts Ana remembers are the interruptions, unfinished jobs and people who had to go back to work halfway through.
agenda: To trade a grand benefit for requested groceries and rides.
family: Tali Harris is Ana’s second cousin. Ana asks what the birthday guest would like this year. Tali remembers the birthdays. A present that was perfect at sixteen may be completely wrong at forty. They take the trouble of finding out. Asked about *The salon on strike*, Tali says, “I own the salon. I used to complain about my own boss doing exactly this, which the oldest technician remembers.”
connections: Amos Ferraro. The director discovers practical help the family would rather have than another performance.

reactions.situation: The understudy is offered the lead before the announcement
reactions.response: Ana asks that the lead singer hear the change directly before it is advertised.

reactions.situation: A cyclist goes down in a crowded crossing
reactions.response: Ana moves the onlookers' bags out of the way, asks the rider what hurts, and asks one named bystander to call for help.
